Title: Man shot by Border Patrol in Portland, Oregon, is charged with aggravated assault on federal officer for alleged car attack - Local News 8

Summary: 
On January 13, 2026, a Border Patrol agent shot Luis David Nino-Moncada and Yorlenys Betzabeth Zambrano-Contreras during a traffic stop in Portland, Oregon, after authorities alleged the driver attempted to weaponize his vehicle. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) stated the incident occurred during a targeted stop of two Venezuelan migrants linked to the Tren de Aragua gang, with Nino-Moncada repeatedly reversing and accelerating his red truck, striking an unoccupied Border Patrol vehicle multiple times. According to the affidavit, one agent fired a defensive shot after fearing for his life, injuring Nino-Moncada in the arm and Zambrano-Contreras in the chest. Nino-Moncada, who illegally entered the U.S. in 2022, was charged with aggravated assault on a federal officer with a deadly or dangerous weapon and depredation of federal property exceeding $1,000. Zambrano-Contreras, who entered in 2023, is also a suspected Tren de Aragua member and allegedly involved in a prostitution ring and a prior Portland shooting. Both were released by the Biden administration. The FBI is leading the investigation, while Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield launched a separate state probe into potential overreach by federal officers. Portland Mayor Keith Wilson called for ICE to halt operations in the city, and Oregon Governor Tina Kotek demanded a full investigation. Protesters gathered at an ICE facility, resulting in six arrests and minor injuries to officers. No body-camera footage or surveillance footage was recovered. DHS initially claimed the two were married, but later corrected that statement. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is assisting the FBI. The incident follows a fatal shooting in Minneapolis the previous day, fueling national concern over federal immigration enforcement tactics.

Title: 2 protesters charged with biting Border Patrol agents after Pretti killing

Summary: 
Two protesters, Emily Duchateau Baierl and Claire Louise Feng, have been charged with assaulting U.S. Border Patrol agents following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti in Minneapolis on January 25, 2026. According to court documents, agents were maintaining a perimeter on Nicollet Avenue between 27th and 28th streets after Pretti’s death. Baierl was apprehended after throwing objects, including chemical agents used by law enforcement, at officers. The incident occurred during a protest following the fatal shooting of 37-year-old U.S. citizen Alex Pretti. Title: Federal immigration officials privately fume over DHS claims after deadly Minnesota shooting

Summary: 
Federal immigration enforcement officials are internally divided over the Department of Homeland Security's (DHS) public messaging following a deadly Border Patrol shooting in Minneapolis on a Saturday morning, where a Border Patrol agent fatally shot Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old Veterans Affairs nurse, who was armed with a handgun and two magazines. DHS officials publicly labeled Pretti a 'domestic terrorist' and claimed he was attempting to 'inflict maximum damage' or carry out a 'massacre,' language that has drawn sharp internal criticism. Multiple federal law enforcement officials told Fox News they believe DHS rushed to judgment, undermining credibility and morale. Some officials described the response as 'a case study on how not to do crisis PR,' with one saying they are 'fed up' and wish to retire, another stating 'DHS is making the situation worse,' and a third asserting 'DHS is wrong' and that 'we are losing this war, we are losing the base and the narrative.' Officials expressed frustration that DHS routinely blames the Border Patrol—a separate agency—for actions it attributes to the broader immigration enforcement effort. The internal friction has intensified debates over DHS leadership’s handling of politically charged incidents, with concerns that aggressive rhetoric is damaging public support for the mass deportation agenda and endangering federal agents. DHS defended its actions, stating, 'We have seen a highly coordinated campaign of violence against our law enforcement,' and that it provides 'swift, accurate information' as new facts emerge. This marks a resurgence of internal tensions previously reported in October 2025 during the Trump administration’s mass deportation initiative.

Published date: January 26 2026, 03:06

Source: Fox News

Reporting voice: Investigative

Title: Border Patrol Pulling Back in Minnesota After Minneapolis Shooting: Reports

Summary: 
Following the fatal shooting of 37-year-old Alex Pretti in south Minneapolis on Saturday, January 25, 2026, some U.S. Border Patrol agents are expected to begin pulling back from Minnesota as early as Monday, January 26, according to The Associated Press. CBS News Minnesota reported that federal immigration agents from Customs and Border Protection (CBP) were involved in the incident, with two U.S. officials confirming that some agents had body cameras, which are being used to reconcile witness accounts with official narratives. The Justice Department is investigating the shooting, which ABC News described as the second fatal shooting of a U.S. citizen in Minneapolis this month involving federal agents, intensifying national scrutiny over federal use-of-force standards. The White House confirmed three federal investigations are underway: a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and FBI probe, and an internal CBP review. President Donald Trump stated he had a 'very good call' with Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, and the White House announced the appointment of border czar Tom Homan to oversee immigration operations in Minnesota—framed as a 'command reset' amid protests, lawsuits, and two high-profile shootings. The reported agent pullback, paired with Homan’s appointment and Trump’s outreach to Walz, is interpreted by allies as a strategic pivot toward centralized control, disciplined enforcement, and visible investigations to de-escalate tensions. Internal frustration within DHS has been reported, with officials concerned that public statements have outpaced confirmed facts. Meanwhile, a federal judge in Minneapolis heard arguments on Monday as Minnesota sued the Trump administration, alleging unconstitutional immigration raid tactics. Democrats are signaling they may use the January 30 deadline to avert a government shutdown to demand greater transparency and oversight of DHS operations. Separately, a person has been federally charged for biting off the tip of a CBP officer’s finger during the unrest, highlighting the escalation into broader street-level violence.

Title: Who Is Jonathan Ross, ICE Officer Who Fatally Shot 37-Year-Old Woman In Minneapolis?

Summary: 
Jonathan Ross, an Iraq war veteran and nearly 20-year veteran of the U.S. Border Patrol and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), has been identified as the federal agent who fatally shot 37-year-old Renee Good in Minneapolis on January 8, 2026. According to records obtained by the Associated Press, Ross joined the Border Patrol in 2007 near El Paso, Texas, and served as a machine gunner during a 2004–2005 deployment with the Indiana National Guard in Iraq. He later worked as a field intelligence agent focused on cartel and smuggling operations. Since transferring to ICE in Minnesota in 2015, Ross has served in fugitive operations, participated in the FBI’s Joint Terrorism Task Force, and trained in firearms and active-shooter response. He was seriously injured in June 2025 when a suspect fled in a vehicle, dragging him down a street; the suspect was later convicted of assaulting a federal officer. DHS Secretary Kristi Noem confirmed the incident, and Vice President JD Vance praised the agent, stating he 'deserves a debt of gratitude.' Federal authorities have not publicly confirmed Ross’s identity, citing safety concerns. The FBI is investigating the shooting, which occurred after Ross believed Good was attempting to run him over. Video footage has raised questions about the use of deadly force. The incident has sparked protests calling for criminal charges, and Minnesota authorities have initiated a review of the case.

Published date: January 09 2026, 06:19

URL: https://www.news18.com/world/who-is-jonathan-ross-ice-officer-who-fatally-shot-37-year-old-woman-in-minneapolis-ws-l-9819284.html
Source: News18
Classification: Crime

Continent: North America

Title: Visual investigation of Minnesota shooting at odds with official statements

Summary: 
On January 26, 2026, videos emerged showing the fatal shooting of 37-year-old Alex Pretti, an American ICU nurse and lawful gun permit holder, by a Border Patrol agent during a protest in Minneapolis. The incident occurred around 9 a.m. Saturday, following a federal immigration operation. Videos verified by CBS News depict Pretti, who was filming the scene with his phone in his right hand and his left hand empty, being pushed by an officer in a tactical vest. Multiple bystanders, including Pretti, were pepper-sprayed and physically restrained. One video shows an agent in a gray jacket removing a gun from Pretti’s waistband before firing the first shot. At least 10 shots were fired by law enforcement. Federal officials, including Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, claimed Pretti approached officers with a 9mm semiautomatic handgun and reacted violently, justifying the use of lethal force. However, sworn witness statements submitted in federal court directly contradict this narrative: one witness stated Pretti had no gun, was not resisting, and was trying to help another protester up; another, a pediatrician, said she saw no weapon, no attack, and no justification for lethal force. Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey described the scene as 'more than six masked agents pummeling one of our constituents, shooting him to death,' and Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz called the videos 'sickening.' The videos and witness accounts raise serious questions about the official account of the shooting.

Published date: January 26 2026, 16:16

Title: Greg Bovino to leave Minneapolis in ICE leadership shake-up

Summary: 
Gregory Bovino, currently serving as the Border Patrol official in charge of on-the-ground immigration enforcement in Minneapolis, is expected to leave the city following two fatal shootings involving federal agents. The incidents include the deaths of Renee Nicole Good, killed by a federal agent in her car, and Alex Pretti, a nurse who was shot by agents and falsely claimed by Bovino to be planning an attack on officers. President Trump announced that his border czar, Tom Homan, will assume direct oversight of on-the-ground operations in Minneapolis and report directly to him. Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey confirmed a phone call with Trump and stated that some federal agents will begin departing the city on Tuesday, though the exact number was not disclosed. According to the New York Times, Trump also spoke with Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, signaling a shift from previous rhetoric that criticized victims to a more cooperative tone. Trump confirmed that Homan will contact Walz to coordinate ICE operations. The leadership changes follow significant unrest in Minneapolis over the immigration enforcement crackdown.
